_headline: SPEED IS NOT THE LIMITER. Three speeds, ONE PIXEL of spread. The 24px shortfall is geometric, and the peak angles say where.
_protocol: identical: grounded-asserted at x1350 (settles y557, y_vel 0, angle $00, plane A), gsp set, sustained held LEFT. Max climb = minimum y.

the_finding.speed_independence: 453 / 454 / 454 across $600, $700, $800. A 33% speed increase buys ONE PIXEL. Momentum is not what stops him.
the_finding.where_he_stops: peak angles cluster $32-$40. $40 is VERTICAL. So the leftward climb dies at or just before the vertical section of the left arc.
the_finding.the_control_says_it_is_passable: rightward peaks at angle $A0 — PAST vertical, into the inverted run. The same player at the same speed gets beyond vertical on the right arc and cannot on the left.
the_finding.therefore: the left arc between the ramp's join and vertical is where the difference lives. Whether that is the ramp's slope, a discontinuity at the join, or the arc's own fit above it, is aurora's to read from the bytes — this measurement narrows it to that span and to the approach to $40, without anyone guessing.

_no_speed_completes: none of $600/$700/$800 completes a leftward circuit, so per the ruling I am stopping here and handing the angles to aurora rather than proceeding to the rule comparison, which still has no completing leftward circuit to run on.
